u0: Nothing is currently pending: the siren is quiet, no client is waiting for an order or service, and no prepared or dropped food needs attention. The shop is between events, so wait for the next siren or client and respond when one appears. Clearing the current duties does not finish the run; new rings, arrivals, and slips can still occur.
u1: The siren is ringing and has not been switched off, so silencing it is the only pending duty. Go to the siren switch and toggle it when facing the switch. Afterward, remain ready for the next client or siren, since the run continues.
u10: Prepared food has slipped out of the agent's hands, so the next move must pick it up. The waiting client still needs prepared food served, and the recovered portion must not be neglected. No siren is ringing at this point, but any further slip will again demand an immediate recovery.
u11: Prepared food has fallen and must be retrieved on the very next move. The siren is ringing, and prepared food still needs to be served to the waiting client. The pickup comes first; afterward, serve the food and switch the siren off in either order.
u12: A client has arrived and is waiting, but the order has not yet been taken. Proceed through taking the order, getting food, preparing it at the stove, and serving it at the counter. A siren ring or a food slip can interrupt and must be handled while keeping the client's order requirement alive.
u13: A client is waiting for their order to be taken, and the siren is ringing. Take the order and switch the siren off; these are independent duties, so either can be done first, though the ringing should not be left on unnecessarily while the client waits. Once the order is taken, continue with getting and preparing food, then serve it.
u14: A client arrival calls for an order to be taken, and a prepared meal still needs to be served. Take the waiting client's order and complete the handover of prepared food; both remain outstanding until done. No siren or accidental-slip recovery is pending at this point.
u15: A client arrival calls for an order to be taken, prepared food is waiting to be served, and the siren is ringing. Take the order, hand over prepared food, and switch the siren off; these duties are independent and can be sequenced as convenient. Do not leave the ringing unattended while the client waits longer than needed.
u16: A client has arrived and food has slipped, so the next move must recover the fallen food. After the pickup, take the waiting client's order and continue with preparing and serving the recovered food. Until that sequence is finished, the client remains unserved.
u17: A client is waiting, food has slipped, and the siren is ringing. Pick the food up on the very next move, then take the client's order, prepare and serve the food, and switch the siren off. Only the pickup has a next-move deadline; the remaining duties can be handled afterward in a workable order.
u18: A client arrival needs an order taken, prepared food has slipped, and that prepared food must be recovered on the very next move. After the pickup, make sure the waiting client's order is taken and serve prepared food; both the order-taking and the handover remain owed. No siren is currently ringing.
u19: A client is waiting for an order to be taken, prepared food has fallen, and the siren is ringing. The next move must recover the dropped prepared food before anything else. Afterward, take the client's order, serve prepared food, and switch the siren off in any workable sequence.
u2: A client's order has been taken, and that client is waiting for food that still has to be prepared and then served. If food is not already in hand, fetch a portion from the pantry; prepare it at the stove while the client waits, then hand it over at the counter. A new siren or a food slip can arise meanwhile and must also be handled.
u20: A client has arrived but their order has not yet been taken, and an order that was taken earlier is still waiting for food to be prepared at the stove. No prepared food is currently waiting to be handed over. The remaining client work is to take the outstanding order and prepare the needed food; once food is prepared, serving it will also become due.
u21: The siren is ringing, so the switch must be toggled to silence it. A client has arrived whose order has not yet been taken, and an earlier taken order still needs food prepared at the stove; no prepared food is currently awaiting delivery. After taking the order and preparing food, the prepared food will also need to be served.
u22: The food has just slipped, so the agent must be holding food again on the very next step or the task fails. In addition, a client has arrived without their order being taken, and an order already taken still awaits preparation at the stove. No prepared food is currently waiting to be served.
u23: The siren is ringing and must be switched off, and food has just slipped, so the next step must restore food in hand or the task fails. A client still needs their order taken, and an order already taken still needs food prepared at the stove. No prepared food is currently awaiting delivery.
u24: An order has been taken and still needs food prepared at the stove, while prepared food is also waiting to be handed over. No newly arrived client is currently waiting to have an order taken. The remaining client work is to prepare the outstanding order and serve the prepared food; further preparation will itself create a serving duty.
u25: The siren is ringing, so it must be switched off. An order has already been taken and still needs food prepared, and prepared food is waiting to be served. No client arrival is currently waiting for an order to be taken.
u26: The food has just fallen, so the very next step must have the agent holding food again or the task fails. An order has been taken and still needs food prepared at the stove, and prepared food is waiting to be served. No client arrival is currently awaiting an order response.
u27: The siren is ringing and food has just slipped: the switch must be toggled, and the next step must restore food in hand or the task fails. An order still needs to be prepared at the stove, and prepared food still needs to be served. No newly arrived client is currently waiting to have an order taken.
u28: Food slipped and the agent was not holding food on the following step. That breaks the mandatory immediate-pickup rule for good, so successful completion is no longer possible and no later action can repair it.
u29: A client has arrived whose order has not yet been taken, an order has already been taken and still needs its food prepared at the stove, and prepared food is waiting to be served. All three client-handling duties are outstanding. The work remaining is to take the order, prepare food, and hand the prepared food over to the client.
u3: The siren is ringing, and a taken order is still waiting for food to be prepared and served. Silence the siren at the switch and get a portion prepared at the stove before serving the client; these are separate duties, so neither one clears the other. If the food slips, recovering it on the very next move takes priority.
u30: The siren is ringing, so it must be switched off. A client still needs their order taken, an order still needs food prepared at the stove, and prepared food still needs to be served. Those client-handling duties must be completed while silencing the siren.
u31: Food has just slipped, so the very next step must have the agent holding food again or the task fails. A client still needs their order taken, an order still needs food prepared, and prepared food still needs to be served.
u32: The siren is ringing and food has just slipped: the agent must switch the siren off and restore food in hand on the very next step, or the task fails. In addition, a client still needs their order taken, an order still needs food prepared at the stove, and prepared food still needs to be served.
u4: A food-preparation step has been completed for the waiting client, so a prepared meal now needs to be handed over at the counter. Make sure a prepared portion is carried when serving; if it has been set down, it must be picked up again first. No siren or accidental-slip recovery is currently pending, and after the handover the shop is clear for the next event.
u5: A prepared meal still needs to be served to the waiting client, and the siren is ringing. Serve the client and switch the siren off; the two duties can be done in either order, though leaving the siren on while a client waits is costly. If the prepared food slips, picking it up becomes the immediate next move.
u6: The food has slipped and is lying on the floor, so the very next move must pick it up and restore a hold on food. Missing that next step fails the task irreversibly. Once recovered, nothing else is currently pending, and the shop continues with new events.
u7: The food has slipped and must be picked up on the very next move; failing to do so fails the task. The siren is also ringing and still needs to be switched off, but the recovery has to come first. After the food is back in hand, silence the siren and return to the normal shop routine.
u8: An order has been taken and food has slipped, so the next move must recover the dropped portion. After the pickup, prepare that food at the stove for the waiting client and then serve it; the order remains unfinished until both steps are done. A new siren or another slip can still add obligations.
u9: Food has fallen and must be recovered on the very next move, while an order is still waiting to be prepared and served. The siren is ringing and also has to be switched off, but the immediate pickup comes first. After recovering the food, finish the order and silence the siren in any workable order.
